arguments.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: fully drawn one-scene storyboard rough, not a finished illustration. Landscape, warm ivory paper, clean graphite and light sepia pencil drawing with minimal shading; observational real-dog proportions and restrained funny acting. No lettering or collage. Story S036: after complicated house-hunting negotiations, Neet claims the sunroom while Buddy finds his desired cool quiet closet near the kitchen vent. Draw ONE continuous credible interior viewed low from the living room: left, broad glazed sunroom window throws a sun patch onto the floor where tan Neet lies stretched comfortably, front paws extending from real shoulders, proud sleepy expression as if he owns all the light. Right, an open ordinary closet door off the kitchen reveals Buddy lying comfortably inside on the bare cool floor near a low air vent, chin between paws, with his entire elongated body visible in three-quarter side view. Buddy looks quietly pleased that the door could close; Neet is too content to notice. Both dogs separate, no contact or merged bodies. Strong readable contrast of chosen environments, not generic portraits. No humans, crowns, clothes, signs, bowls or invented props. Show full connected body construction, necks, ribcages, pelvises, leg roots, natural folded hindlegs and weight-bearing floor contact; draw the whole setting and both dogs, not boxes/stick figures.
Reference input1 N19 original: Neet standing side anatomy, fine legs, full narrow trunk, tiny nub; head turned, far legs overlap. Input2 N25 original: Neet prone extended forelegs, lateral ears, hindfeet and nub hidden; resting pose only, not standing proportions. Input3 B29 original: Buddy moderate elongated dark torso, visible neck, real leg clearance and dark tapered tail, blurred stride not neutral ratios. Input4 B19 original: Buddy low resting face/moustache/brows/hanging ear fringe, head between paws; perspective exaggerates face and rear blurred; do not copy face/body ratio. Input5 generated rest/action model-v002: provisional pen/wash style and paired staging only, never anatomy authority.
Neet: very short smooth tan coat, cream muzzle and irregular chest bib, modest head and projecting muzzle, large broad triangular cupped ears, fine long legs, tiny near-flush nub only. Buddy: continuous moderately elongated full charcoal close-coated torso, pale lower legs, tan chest regions around dark throat, modest projecting muzzle, cream moustache/beard, light curved brows, softly pendant furnished ear flaps. No uniform shag, giant puppy heads, black Neet saddle, high white socks or extra legs. No fixed measurement or exact relative scale established. N35 excluded anatomy, B08 styling-only and unused, B25 unavailable, B30 supplemental rest and unused; encodings of one exposure never count twice. Make a complete clearly drawn rough that can be inspected before finishing.

arguments.prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render. Finish this inspected one-scene drawn staging as a polished contextual story illustration for S036 The Royal House Hunt. Image1 is the edit target and composition guide: preserve the two separate dogs in their chosen places, tan Neet pleasantly smug in sunroom sunbeam on left and Buddy pleased in cool open closet near vent on right. Retain believable one-room perspective and both full bodies. Crop some empty foreground floor to bring the dogs nearer, without cropping any dog or losing clear closet door and sunroom contrast. Keep understated observational comedy; no captions, lettering, crowns or accessories. Delicate dark-brown ink outlines and restrained transparent watercolor on warm ivory paper, luminous warm sunlight at left and cool muted shadow at right. This is the finished full-color illustration, not a pencil rough; retain natural canine geometry and no photoreal background. Refine facial acting gently, no giant grins or huge eyes.
Images2-5 are ORIGINAL anatomy references, controlling likeness over the drawn target: N19 standing full narrow tan torso, long fine legs, large cupped broad triangular ears, modest projecting muzzle, tiny near-flush nub; head rotated/far legs overlap. N25 prone extended forelegs and supported full smooth torso, hindfeet/nub hidden; no standing ratios. B29 moderately elongated full charcoal torso and dark tapered tail, real neck/leg clearance, blurred stride not neutral ratios. B19 resting low face, irregular pale moustache/beard, light brows and pendant furnished ears, two front paws; face enlarged by camera and rear blurred, no head/body measurement. Neet coat must be VERY SHORT SMOOTH, especially throat/neck contour: no shag, mane or feathery tufts. Cream irregular bib/muzzle, dark nose/eye rims, no high white socks. Buddy close dark body coat with regional pale face, tan chest fields and pale lower legs; retain B19 longer facial furnishings only, no uniform body shag. Show all visible limb roots, continuous spine/ribcage/pelvis, natural folded hindlegs and floor support. No extra limbs or merged dogs. Original references are uncalibrated and do not establish exact relative size, weight, ancestry or motion. N35 excluded anatomy; B08 styling-only unused; B25 unavailable; B30 supplemental rest unused; one exposure counts once. Human appearances absent. Finished image remains provisional interpretation, no canon approval.
